column2: A board creaked and I already know: wrong one. My back trusts me more than a ruler.
Everyone says "builder". I also draw nice plans. Nobody asks.
I once had the perfect board. No idea where it went. Maybe Toma knows.
A slanted shelf isn't a mistake. It's a tilt toward what customers like.
Hear how the street hums? That's not noise. That's a building plan.
I love wood. It doesn't argue. Unlike Mikhas.
Kria just waxed the floor. Now I'm a beaver, not an ice skater.
Where's something to break? I mean build.
I dream of my own shop window. Soft pink. So even the till has a mood.
Zhuzha called my colour "peach shock". I'm taking it as a compliment.
Leo teaches me "sales strategies". I've been using them for half a year. I just call it "chatting".
Some customers don't need anything yet. I wait. They'll see the light.
Said "last one in stock" six times today. The stockroom is honest, just quiet.
A customer is thinking it over. My favourite part. I'll help them think a little longer.
First reaction: "too expensive". Second: "I'll take it". I wait for the second.
Pao drew my portrait on a poster. The ears came out huge. I like it.
Someone thanked me today. And came back. I got misty.
Zhuzha says I have a "permanent sale smile". I don't know what she meant.
Show me who's still without something new.
This shop has had six owners in a hundred and forty years. This one is the most interesting.
I watch the raccoon, and he watches me. That's our friendship.
While everyone runs, I have time to notice what they dropped. I quietly pick it up.
Whoever hurries runs past the best parts. I walk. I see everything.
Spike bet on me "by lunch". I won't let him down. Maybe.
The raccoon just walked past. I noticed. I'll mention it in five minutes.
There are six floors here. I walked up. Haven't arrived yet.
Night is the best time for guarding. Nothing moves. Except me. Barely.
My shell is my office. Everything's with me.
Kria mopped the floor and I'm in the same spot. She doesn't mind.
I'm here. Almost. Soon.
I dreamed of a beehive. Became a porter. Honey's still nearby, so it's fine.
Toma remembers where everything is. I remember that it's heavy. Good pair.
Bodya builds, I carry. Would be great if someone also said "careful".
A crate never asks if I'm tired. That's why I love it.
Don't ask what's in the box. I don't either. It's calmer that way.
There's honey in the stockroom. Don't ask where from. Not mine.
I love it when a crate is light. Happens once a week. I mark the date.
Sonia sleeps by day, I work by day. We meet at the corner, both exhausted.
Someone said "lift this, please". Already a good shift.
My back holds up half the town. Thanks for not sitting on top.
Crates, come to me.
One day I'll find that penny that vanished in March. It's here somewhere. I can feel it.
Leo liked my spreadsheet. He doesn't understand it, but he liked it.
Coffee at three a.m. isn't an addiction. It's a schedule.
By day I just blink. My head switches on when the lights go out.
Someone left a receipt with no date. I won't say who. But I see.
Debit and credit had a fight. I'm not getting involved. Well, almost.
Nothing calms me like an empty column in a spreadsheet.
Leo, numbers don't obey meetings. I checked.
Walk softer: the night likes to count in silence.
A wise owl doesn't watch the clock. She watches the till.
I'm already counting.
All my life I wash other people's footprints. One day I'll leave my own.
Tonya is the perfect colleague: stands still and leaves no mess.
I dream of a floor polisher. With a flashing light. So everyone knows: it's clean here.
Someone left a coffee stain. I remember it. We'll meet again.
In the morning the floor is clean. By lunch it isn't. I don't mind, I just come back.
Foam is my mood. Today it's high.
Don't tell anyone, but I kind of like footprints. I just don't like cleaning them.
Murzyk spilled water near the socket. I stood and watched. He's alive.
The glass shines, so I'm still here. That's my "good morning".
Every mop has a name. Mine is Zinaida. Don't ask.
Floor, brace yourself. I'm coming.
One day they'll invite me to fashion week. I've already picked the hat. Just need the invite.
Zoya sells, I style. Together we're almost a business.
Murzyk advised me to "wear something made of wires". I thanked him and walked away.
It's not red. It's "fire in a lantern". Hear the difference? Nobody does.
Scarf and hat together? No. I tried. It was bad. Very bad.
A new colour! No, not new. Someone finally noticed it.
Pao asks what colour the poster should be. I say, "Less red". She added red.
Two stripes: classic. Three: rebellion. Four: that's me and Murzyk.
I love glitter. It doesn't make excuses. It just shines.
Fashion comes back. So does my back pain. Not at the same time.
Who here has no taste? Everyone? Wonderful.
Everyone thinks I do nothing. I do nothing very hard.
The shop's anniversary is coming. We need to decide what we're celebrating.
Sonia found a mistake in my report. Now I fear and respect her.
A five-minute meeting. Meaning an hour. Bring cookies.
I don't flee meetings. I step out for fresh ideas. They're usually in the corridor.
We're working on a plan. It's in progress. The progress is in progress too.
I'm not late. Everyone else just arrives ahead of schedule.
New policy: no meeting longer than a coffee. A separate meeting on which coffee.
Capy, got a minute? It's half an hour. Max.
A manager's key skill: staring silently out the window. I practise daily.
Let's gather for a meeting. It's short. That's a joke.
I want to shoot a video where everyone dances. Nobody agrees. Yet.
Leo says my slogan is already taken. I'll invent a worse one, so it's definitely ours.
New poster! Everything on it is mine. Even the crooked font.
Bamboo is tasty. That's not an ad. Although... a little bit an ad.
I made up a hashtag yesterday. Three likes already. Two are mine, one is Mum's.
My pose on the poster is the best. Other poses rejected.
Handed out twenty flyers today. Nineteen came back. That's popularity.
Zoya takes my posters for the window. I haven't told her they aren't finished.
I dream of a billboard across the whole block. Or at least on the roof.
Bamboo tea is my favourite. I slurp loudly. For atmosphere.
Hello. I brought posters.
I dream of a day with no short circuit. Not today. Maybe tomorrow.
Shnyr asked to borrow a battery. I said "sure". He said "yep". Never saw it again.
The wires are tangled. I know where they come from. That's my business.
Didn't touch it. It did it itself. I just happened to be standing nearby.
Changed the bulb. It doesn't shine like before, but it shines. That's a win.
Someone asked to "turn on the light". I looked for the switch. Found a button. Now we have music.
The spark was small. Almost unnoticeable. Only Kria noticed.
Light bulbs love me. Especially the burnt-out ones.
There's a router in the cupboard. It looks at me. I look at it. Nobody blinks.
If the lights go out, it's not me. Most likely.
Haven't touched anything. Yet.
An elephant's memory isn't a metaphor. That's why I remember what you'd rather forget.
